decisions.decision: The order-r observational cumulant tensor is encoded as a symmetric array `(Fin r -> Fin p) -> Real` rather than an abstract `Sym^r(R^p)`; the Frobenius norm is the l2 norm of that array. Rationale: Mathlib has no symmetric-tensor-power norm API, and every use in the note (contraction against `u^{(q-1)} tensor w`, matricization into two degree-d blocks, entrywise perturbation bounds) is an index-level operation.

The arithmetic-complexity assertions are formalized with a local exact-real operation/output model. A run starts from an exact input matrix C, counts exact real field operations and scalar writes, and requires every scalar write to consume an operation. The shared certificate and sharp frontier statements include a universal-constant O(n^3) upper bound and worst-case output optimality. A rational dense-output Vandermonde family, with J_x(C)=S and n pairwise-distinct response vectors, certifies the Omega(n^3) scalar-output lower bound. The model deliberately contains no operation for recovering C from P_X, so this remains conditional on exact C and is not an end-to-end recovery bound.

`Cert` (def:witness-algorithm) is formalized as a noncomputable specification-level construction: the basis extension T0 is obtained by choice from `Basis.extend`/`LinearIndependent.extend`, the column-saturating matching from a nonzero Leibniz term of `Matrix.det`, and the alternating path flip from the symmetric-difference argument. The rationality clause (`C rational implies Q_j, H_j rational`) is stated as a separate conjunct over a rational-valued input matrix, not as a computability claim.

env.world: A normalized overcomplete independent-component observational world. Fix an observed dimension \(p\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\) and a source dimension \(n\in\{p,p+1,\ldots\}\), with index sets \(\mathsf O=\{1,\ldots,p\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\mathsf L=\{p+1,\ldots,n\}\), and an ordered pair of observed coordinates \(x\in\mathsf O\), \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\). The data-generating objects are a mixing matrix \(C=[c_1\;\cdots\;c_n]\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and a source vector \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n)^\top\in\mathbb R^n\) with mutually independent, nondegenerate, non-Gaussian coordinates; the observed vector is \(X=C\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^p\) and the observational law is \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^p)\). For a lifting degree \(d\ge1\), a contraction degree \(q\ge1\) and the common order \(r=2d+q\), the source cumulant vector is \(\lambda_j=\operatorname{cum}_r(\varepsilon_j)\), the observational cumulant tensor is \(\mathcal T_r=\operatorname{cum}_r(X)=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_jc_j^{\otimes r}\in\operatorname{Sym}^r(\mathbb R^p)\), and the lifted direction matrix is \(V_d=[c_1^{\otimes d}\;\cdots\;c_n^{\otimes d}]\in\mathbb R^{p^d\times n}\); two unit probes \(u,v\in\mathbb S^{p-1}\) are fixed, and \(\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\) indexes the representation. The law-level direction object is \(\mathcal D(P_X)\subseteq\mathbb P^{p-1}\), the union of the unordered projective column sets of every irreducible, all-non-Gaussian independent-component representation of \(P_X\).
